# Sluice

> Sluice sends a file or a folder straight from one computer to another over QUIC, checks every
> block against its BLAKE3 root before writing it, and keeps no copy in between. No account, no
> hosted storage, no telemetry. Free and open source, Apache-2.0 or MIT.

Sluice is one engine with three ways in: a command line, a page in a browser that drives a daemon on
the same computer, and a Model Context Protocol server for an AI assistant. Sending and receiving in
a browser with nothing installed, and a desktop app, are planned for 1.2 and are not available.

## Start here

- [Send a file](https://sluicedrop.com/#send): the four steps with a local daemon and its page, today.
- [Three ways in](https://sluicedrop.com/#ways): people, developers, AI agents.
- [How it works](https://sluicedrop.com/#how): the channel, the blocks, and the ticket.
- [For developers](https://sluicedrop.com/developers/): the commands, a real run, and install.
- [For AI agents](https://sluicedrop.com/agents/): the MCP server, its setup and its seven tools.

## Commands and install

- [CLI reference](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/crates/sluice-cli/README.md): every
  command, flag, exit code and JSON field.
- [Install guide](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/docs/install.md): every channel, the
  checks that verify a download, upgrade and uninstall.

## For programs

- [Control API](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/SPEC.md#11-control-api),
  `proto/sluice/v1`: the gRPC calls that the page, the MCP server and scripts use.
- [MCP tools](https://sluicedrop.com/agents/#tools): `sluice mcp --root <folder>`, seven tools over
  standard input and output.
- [Wire specification](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/SPEC.md): tickets, manifests,
  content, live mode, the control API, and test vectors for a compatible implementation.

## Background

- [Design](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/docs/design.md): architecture, data model and
  storage rules.
- [Threat model](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md): what is
  protected, what is not, and the known weaknesses.
- [Decision records](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/tree/main/docs/adr): why each choice was made.
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md) and
  [changelog](https://github.com/sanamhub/sluice/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
